events.summary: President invited private investors to develop official residences as tourist lodges.
Trial runs began for solar-powered waste collection boats on Beira Lake.
US cultural preservation funding supported recovery and documentation of Kodavaya artefacts.
National Transport Commission decided to implement an integrated bus timetable.
Crop insurance compensation was paid to 3,422 Polonnaruwa farmers.
A further compensation tranche was scheduled for 365 affected farmers.
August Aswesuma allowances will be deposited for 599,730 elderly beneficiaries.
UNDP and partners launched livestock insurance to protect Sri Lankan leopards.
President ordered feasibility review for completing 18 abandoned bridge projects in Hambantota.
Second-phase excavation of the Semmani mass grave resumed in Jaffna.
NTC introduced a joint midnight timetable for SLTB and private long-distance buses.
President established a 28-member task force to develop Sri Lanka tourism.
Fingerprint scanner system implemented at Colombo Central Postal Exchange.
Cabinet paper shortened the international coal tender period from six to five weeks.
Government decided to construct 100 telecommunications towers in poorly connected areas.
Government is considering importing double-cab vehicles for MPs and government officials.
Cabinet approved linking government institutions to the National Cyber Security Operations Centre.
Motor vehicle department opens tender for official number plates
Sri Lanka Customs introduces a new registration and declaration system
United States pledges a fourth patrol vessel donation to Sri Lanka
President instructed officials to prepare and submit a comprehensive national sports development plan.
Japan-Sri Lanka Business Environment Committee held its inaugural meeting to address investor problems.
Sayura fisheries life insurance scheme launched in Kudawella for fishing communities.
President promised 2026 budget funding for construction of the Kokkilai-Pulmoddai bridge.
August Aswesuma allowances will be credited to beneficiaries’ bank accounts.
Authorities plan to renovate 45 aging government apartment complexes in Colombo District.
Health Ministry declared August National Breastfeeding Month and held a national celebration.
Cabinet approved major renovation works at the Sri Lankan Parliament complex.
Renovation works are underway across Parliament roofs, facilities and medical centre.
President instructed officials to prepare plans supporting unprofitable rural bus services.
Mannar wind power project activities were temporarily halted for one month for public consultation.
Government planned AI workshops to prepare ministry staff for public-service digitalisation.
Government authorised seven foreign investors to cultivate cannabis under strict conditions.
Minimum investment required for each approved cannabis cultivation investor was stated.
Sri Lanka Police launched a WhatsApp channel for public crime and problem reports.
Transport Ministry announced a pilot to install 40 AI camera systems on buses.
Transport Minister inaugurated installation of 40 AI camera systems on long-distance buses.
Cabinet approved LKR 2 billion for the nationwide District Development Programme.
Cabinet approved recognizing Sabarimala as an official pilgrimage destination and facilitating pilgrims.
Sri Lanka and India scheduled their 2025 bilateral joint naval exercise in Colombo.
Railways announced a weekend express train service between Colombo and Badulla.
Solar-powered cameras and GPS alerts monitor elephant crossings near railway lines.
Prime minister outlined vocational education reforms planned for implementation from 2026.
National Transport Commission relaunched route 155 between Mattakkuliya and Soyzapura.
Construction began on stalls for Indigenous community products.
Sri Lanka’s first Indigenous herbal soap was launched.
Emergency Life Support software app was launched at the medical conference.
Crop insurance compensation was paid for drought, floods and elephant damage.
New app launched to warn users about nearby wild elephant movements.
Mannar wind power development works were decided to be suspended.
Health Ministry invited applications to recruit 1,408 trained doctors.
Wind turbine tower components reached Mannar under police protection amid protests.
Minister halted movement on Mannar wind power project pending a special meeting.
Government proposed low-interest housing loans for public employees.
Railway Department launched special trains for Kandy Esala Perahera visitors.
Prime Minister pledged support to recover and digitise historic Jaffna Library materials.
India provided financing for the first phase of Maho–Anuradhapura railway signalling.
First-phase signalling and telecommunications works have started.
Government proposed reforms integrating vocational education into school education.
Airport service began issuing temporary Sri Lankan driving licences to foreign tourists.
Parliament approved preparations to convert the Speaker’s official residence into a research centre.
First successful government IVF birth reported at North Colombo Teaching Hospital.
